thread:
oliver: quick sync 1 1 prototype for autoscaler follow-up: hybrid local delegates + central coordinator. want sanity checks on failure modes.
kim: high-level responsibilities?
oliver: delegates = immediate admission, short probe-warmups, local headroom accounting. central = persistent lease store, global fairness, mint tokens for admission and long-term reconciler.
maya: state durability concern 1 delegates restarting could miscount.
oliver: delegates keep ephemeral in-memory counters; central persists leases. on delegate start they fetch active leases snapshot. no raft checkpointing in delegates to simplify.
raj: what about network partitions? last canary double-admitted.
oliver: token approach: central mints short-lived admission tokens (default ttl=10s). delegates only admit when token valid. if coordinator unreachable, delegates switch to "local_cautious": rely on cached tokens and conservative headroom.
kim: token flow adds 1 RPC on first admission. acceptable?
oliver: yes, token caching reduces RPCs. alternative was optimistic local admission + compensating evictions, but that causes user-visible failures when reconciler drops sessions.
maya: suggest SDK-friendly errors when admission denied: structured JSON like {"code":"POOL_EXHAUSTED","suggested_action":"downgrade:model-small","retry_after_ms":"1500"}.
raj: burst handling? preemptible noisy neighbors are common.
oliver: design: per-tenant burst credits + shared spillover pool. delegates consume tenant credits then request spillover token from coordinator. if denied, return structured error to SDK.
kim: prewarm heuristics? full prewarm costly.
oliver: probe-warmup: delegate issues tiny probe requests to populate KV cache when queue growth > alpha over window T. default alpha=0.2 over 15s; probe budget per min=10.
maya: eviction flow needs to be graceful 1 reconciler evicted live sessions last time and caused client errors.
oliver: soft-first eviction: 1) stop admitting new burst requests 2) mark draining 3) wait for inflight tokens to expire 4) soft-evict low-priority sessions with 5s pre-notify, fallback to force after deadline. eviction API: POST /v1/evict {"pool":"p1","mode":"soft|force","targets":[ids],"deadline_ms":5000}.
raj: ops emergency drain?
oliver: force requires two approvers and emits audit event: ops-bot: EMERGENCY_DRAIN pool=p1 approvers=[kim,raj].
deploy-bot: deploy queued: autoscaler/delegate v0.3.4 -> canary pool-alpha at 14:00 UTC.
kim: metrics to add: credits_used, local_headroom_free, probe_success_rate, token_mint_latency, reconcile_conflicts_count, evictions_soft_count, evictions_force_count, admission_downgrade_count. add admission_trace_id to logs.
maya: rollout gates: rollback if reconcile_conflicts_count > 5/min or probe_failure_rate > 20% sustained for 10m.
raj: fallback modes for delegates: central_only | local_cautious | optimistic. default local_cautious.
kim: on storage, we avoid raft in delegates; central persists leases and delegates fetch snapshot on start.
oliver: TL;DR decisions: 1) delegates with ephemeral state + token-based admissions, 2) central persists leases and mints short tokens, 3) probe-warmup to reduce full prewarm cost, 4) burst credits + shared spillover, 5) soft-first eviction API + two-approver force, 6) canary gates + automatic rollback triggers.
maya: I'll draft failure-mode playbook and SDK error contract.
kim: I'll build dashboards and alerts for reconcile_conflicts_count.
raj: scheduling 30m follow-up tomorrow to review canary checklist.
oliver: thanks everyone, ping me for edge-cases. :thumbsup:
